topics.name: Transport Handshake Identity
topics.purpose: Define each cryptographic/protocol handshake attempt as explicit transient evidence with negotiated profile, peer proof and result.

semantics.identity_rule: Each handshake attempt has an explicit identity.
semantics.peer_rule: Peer proof/key refs are explicit where available.
semantics.legacy_rule: MD5 handshake usage, where part of historical AIGMos transport compatibility, is explicitly scoped and must never be mistaken for modern cryptographic integrity/authentication strength.
semantics.application_rule: Handshake success precedes but does not replace application authentication/authorization.

invariants.rule: Listener, route, endpoint, connection, channel, peer reachability and cryptographic transport evidence never by themselves grant application, data or operation authority.
Inbound network data remains inert until explicit protocol parsing, validation, identity/context resolution, authorization and dispatcher routing succeed.

hard_gates.condition: MD5 treated as sufficient modern authentication
connection identity reused as handshake identity
